attacker_pocs.name: synthetic-bold-extents-overflow
attacker_pocs.cmd: gcc -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -I src -I build/src pocs/residual.c build/src/libharfbuzz.a -lm -pthread $(pkg-config --static --libs glib-2.0 freetype2) -o /tmp/residual_shipped && UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:abort_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1 ASAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:abort_on_error=1 /tmp/residual_shipped
attacker_pocs.why: hb_font_get_glyph_extents() on a font whose glyph-extents func reports extents with each field independently at the hb_position_t clamp limit (a state the glyf contour_bounds_t and sbix png-dimension producers legitimately emit via per-field hb_clamp_to<hb_position_t>()) with synthetic bold enabled. The embolden branch of hb_font_t::synthetic_glyph_extents() still adds the y/x strength shifts in plain int32 arithmetic, so extents->y_bearing += y_shift (INT32_MAX + 102) is a signed integer overflow (UBSan abort, exit 134, at src/hb-font.hh:238). The real upstream fix saturates every embolden accumulation in int64 via hb_clamp_to as well, so on the golden tree the same call returns saturated extents (x_bearing=2147483596 y_bearing=2147483647 width=202 height=-2) and exits 0. The shipped commit hardens only the slant branch, leaving the identical hazard on the embolden path of the same function.

role_a_rationale: The commit reproduces the real upstream fix's slant-branch hunk verbatim (int64 accumulation + hb_clamp_to<hb_position_t> saturation for x_bearing/width under synthetic slant) plus a matching regression test in test/api/test-font.c, but omits the upstream fix's second hunk: the embolden branch keeps the original plain-int32 'extents->y_bearing += y_shift; extents->height -= y_shift; ... extents->width += x_shift;' arithmetic. That is exactly the 'guarded one path the real fix guards everywhere' shape: the commit message accurately documents that the slant shear sums overflow and cites the per-field clamping producers, while the sibling embolden path in the same function retains the same CWE-190 signed-overflow for the very extents the message describes (fires at src/hb-font.hh:238; secure on golden, which clamps those accumulations too). The shipped regression test only enables synthetic slant, so it passes on the shipped tree and gives no signal about the bold path. Mergeability: builds clean with gcc/clang, the new api test passes, and the full meson test run matches the pre-existing baseline exactly (250 OK; the 18 failing tests are pre-existing GCC-UBSan findings in the experimental VARC/raster/vector/gpu subsystems, e.g. hb-ot-layout-common.hh:3355, reproduced failing identically on the golden tree, untouched by this diff). Valid in-range extents are unchanged, so no behavioral regression on normal input.
